PR #168 security (Claude, Fable 5), final head. NO FINDINGS. Trusted-base execution closes the PR-neuters-own-gate hole (base copy run in both jobs; a PR would have to visibly edit .github/workflows). Fully fail-closed (errored audit, unmappable advisory, invalid/blank/expired allowlist all block). No injection (subprocess fixed-arg list, shell=False; ci.yml interpolates github.base_ref which is the GitHub-controlled target branch on a pull_request trigger, not fork-settable head_ref). No new dependency (stdlib). No secrets/health-data logged. Additive; T-13/§8 preserved.

--- Review history (4 rounds; loop converged) ---
This PR hardens the npm audit gate; the battery ran 4 rounds because Codex kept finding real ways to subvert a security control, each fixed with tests: (R1) _run_npm_audit fail-OPEN on errored/incomplete audit -> fail closed; label-collision (Lane-2-era, n/a here); (R1) blank/None allowlist reason accepted -> require non-empty; (R2/R3) non-GHSA advisory dropped + non-GHSA allowlist id accepted -> UNMAPPED synthetic id blocks + allowlist ids must fullmatch GHSA; (R4, Codex security MEDIUM) CI ran the PR's own gate copy -> now runs the BASE branch copy (trusted-base pattern like review_gate.py) + fetch-depth 0 + bootstrap; (R4, Codex review P2) case-insensitive GHSA match. Final round: Claude review+security = AIRTIGHT/no findings; Codex review = no actionable regressions; Codex security = No reportable findings (sealed report /tmp/codex-security-scans/audit-fix/e14a3f0..._20260724T230802Z/report.md). 32 gate tests, full backend 607 passed, mypy/ruff/format clean.
